REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE   

 This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm’s ability to submit a proposal should formal solicitation be issued in the future. 

 NAICS Code: 236220 – Commercial and Institutional Building Construction 

  (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.)  

 Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million 

  PROJECT OVERVIEW  

 The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), in support of U.S. Army Materiel Command (AMC), IMCOM Directorate – Sustainment, and USAG Fort Belvoir, has a requirement for the design and construction of a project to restore and modernize Building 1809 located at 6020 30th Engineer Road, Fort Belvoir, Fairfax County, Virginia (22060-5200). The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary design services, equipment, materials, labor, construction management, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver a fully functional, modernized, and code-compliant administrative and general-purpose storage facility on the Installation. 

 Building 1809 was placed in service on July 24, 1961, and has exceeded its original 40-year estimated useful life. The asset is a single-story (1 floor above ground, 0 floors below ground, 20 feet in height), semi-permanent concrete structure (Construction Material Code: CONC; Structure Code: S20; Roof Code: R11; Wall Code: W25) comprising a total of 26,247 Square Feet (SF) with a design capacity of 76 persons (PN). The facility is configured for dual-purpose operations: 

 
	  Administrative Building, General Purpose (Category Code 61050):  16,014.61 SF (Design Capacity: 76 PN), supporting Air Force / U.S. Special Operations Command (AFELM US SOCOM, UIC: FFDY01). 
	  Storage Building, General Purpose, Installation (Category Code 44220):  10,232.66 SF, supporting USAG Fort Belvoir (UIC: W4VNAA). 
 

 Despite a 100% utilization rate and a Mission Critical (Readiness Tier T1) designation, the facility currently holds a Current Use Functionality Capability Code of F3, indicating a significant requirement for restoration and modernization funds to make the asset capable of meeting the function for which it is used. Furthermore, the asset holds a Facility Physical Quality Code of Q4 (Physical Quality Rating: 57), meaning the sum of all necessary restoration and modernization costs is greater than 40 percent of the Plant Replacement Value (PRV).

 Key facility deficiencies and modernization requirements include: 

 
	  Fire Protection & Life Safety:  The building is currently classified under Facility Fire Rating Code 1 ( Unsprinklered Combustible ). Comprehensive fire suppression and life safety upgrades are required to meet current UFC and NFPA codes. 
	  HVAC & Mechanical Systems:  While the building is serviced by water, sewer, electrical, and telephone utilities, it currently lacks air conditioning ( Air Conditioning: N ). Modernized HVAC and climate control systems are required to support administrative personnel and storage preservation. 
	  Accessibility & Sustainability:  The facility has not yet been evaluated for ADA compliance ( Code: NEVL ) or Sustainability ( Code: 3 – Not Yet Evaluated ). Full architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) modernization is needed to achieve code compliance, energy efficiency, and operational resilience. 
	  Historic Status:  Determined Not Eligible for Listing (DNE, evaluated January 7, 2016). 
	  Metering:  There are currently no utility metering records associated with this asset; smart utility metering integration will be required. 
 

 Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $10-12M 

   PRIMARY ACQUISITION STRATEGY UNDER EVALUATION   :  Progressive Design Build (PDB) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA). 

 The Louisville District is evaluating a Progressive Design Build (PDB) strategy utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 2808a. This authority authorizes transactions other than standard contracts to carry out facility repair and construction projects – including planning, design, engineering, piloting and execution – enabling early contractor involvement, commercial pricing transparency, and schedule and cost efficiencies.
